text: How poor versus rich people buy a house.
Benny saves for years. The bank says: you're approved for four hundred thousand.
So he buys the biggest house that number gets him. Four bedrooms. Two-car garage.
But the bank looked at his pay before taxes. Not his grocery bill.
The payment is over three thousand a month. More than half his take-home pay.
Then the furnace dies. Six thousand dollars, on a credit card.
Now he eats noodles on the floor of a four-hundred-thousand-dollar house. That's house poor.
Rick gets the same approval letter. But he buys a duplex. Two homes, one building.
He uses an FHA loan. Three and a half percent down, if he lives in one side.
On a three-hundred-thousand-dollar duplex, that's ten thousand five hundred, plus closing costs.
He rents the other side for fifteen hundred. His payment is about twenty-five hundred.
So Rick lives there for about a thousand a month. Less than a one-bedroom apartment.
A year later, he moves out and rents both sides.
But if a renter leaves, or the roof leaks, Rick pays. Being a landlord is a real job.
Same bank. Opposite house. Which one would you buy?
